questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My ______ car is parked near the tree.
questions.s:
Among the given options, option (b) 'fathers'' denotes the possession by multiple persons whereas the sentence has the possessive determiner 'my' which means there can be only one father for a person. So, options (b) and (c) (fathers' and fathers) are eliminated. Option (d), 'father' is a common noun which is not in a possessive form and so, it is also negated. Option (a), 'father's' is the most appropriate possessive form of the noun that can fill the given blank as required.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

The complete sentence is: My father's car is parked near the tree.

questions.q:
In the question given below, one part of the sentence may or may not have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

Measle is a highly contagious(A)/ virus that lives in the(B)/ nose and throat mucus(C)/ of an infected person(D).
questions.s:
Part A has an error. There are certain nouns which apparently seem plural but are in fact singular. These include the names of some common diseases like mumps, rickets etc. 'Measles' is one such word. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence would be: Measles is a highly contagious virus that lives in the nose and throat mucus of an infected person.

questions.q: Two and a half hour/ (a) have passed since/(b) I returned from my village /(c)/ no error/(d)
o: Two and a half hour
I returned from my village
questions.s: After "two and a half," the noun must be plural because the quantity exceeds one. Change "hour" to "hours". "Two and a half hours have passed." Any fraction or decimal greater than 1 requires a plural noun.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

My father gave me a very useful advice before I left for my first job interview, telling me to be confident, honest, and to listen carefully to every question asked.
o: a very useful piece of advice
questions.s:
The error lies in the noun that follows the phrase "One of the". This phrase is always followed by a plural noun or pronoun because it refers to a single item chosen from a group of many. In the given sentence, "requirement" is a singular noun, which is grammatically incorrect in this context. It should be the plural noun "requirements".

Correct sentence: One of the key requirements for this job is proficiency in at least two languages.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option d).

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.q:
The student's knowing of the subject astonished the teacher.

[MTS 20/08/2019 S3]
questions.s:
• "Student's knowing" is incorrect because "knowing" is a present participle/gerund and does not fit in the sentence. The abstract noun "knowledge" should be used instead to indicate the student's understanding of the subject.

  • The sentence focuses on the subject knowledge of the student, it should be"student's knowledge".

Correct sentence: The student's knowledge of the subject astonished the teacher.

questions.q:
Tons of sheep were grazing in the field.

[CHSL 20/10/2020 S3]
questions.s:
• The phrase "tons of sheep" is incorrect when referring to a group of sheep. The correct collective noun for sheep is "a flock of sheep."

  • "sheep" is both singular and plural, so terms like "sheeps" are grammatically incorrect.

Corrected Sentence: A flock of sheep was grazing in the field.

questions.q: I like (1)/ the poetries (2)/ of Byron and Shelley. (3)/ No error (4).

questions.s: "Poetry" is an uncountable noun. "The poetry" is correct.

questions.q: Regular brushing and flossing are essential for maintaining healthy tooth and gums.
questions.s:
The sentence should use the plural form "teeth" instead of the singular "tooth" to match the plural subject "regular brushing and flossing." Additionally, "gums" should also remain plural to match "teeth."

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "Regular brushing and flossing are essential for maintaining healthy teeth and gums."

questions.q: The doctor advised him to lose a weight of pound to reduce strain on his knees.
o: to reduce strain on his knees
to lose a weight of pound
questions.s:
We can use apostrophes with the nouns related to ‘time/weight/place’. So, pound’s weight is the correct one instead of ‘weight of pound.’

Therefore, the correct sentence would be: “The doctor advised him to lose a pound’s weight to reduce strain on his knees.”

questions.s:
The phrase "true to her word" is an idiomatic expression meaning to keep a promise or commitment. "Words" should be a singular "word" in this context.

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "Despite the challenges, she remained true to her word and completed the project on time."

questions.q: Eighty–five thousand rupees (1)/ is a large sum of money (2)/ to earn in a month. (3)/ No error (4)

questions.s: To show possession for two separate owners, each name needs its own apostrophe and "s."So, it should be "Ram’s and Sita’s house," not "Ram’s and Sita’ house."

questions.q:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.

Every person should know their own _________, what their skill set is and how unique they are.
questions.s:
The blank requires a noun to describe what a person owns. Let's look at the meanings of the given words.

Calamities: an event causing great and often sudden damage or distress; a disaster.

Punctualities: the fact or quality of being on time.

Specialties: a particular type of work that they do most or do best, or a subject that they know a lot about.

Fecundities: the ability to produce an abundance of offspring or new growth; fertility.

The sentence talks about a person's attributes and uniqueness. Therefore, among the given options, 'specialties' is the most appropriate choice.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q: The little boy (did many mischiefs) in school. (CGL Mains- 02/08/2022)
questions.s: "Mischief" is generally an uncountable noun. "Much mischief" or "a lot of mischief" is correct.

questions.q: An earthquake is/(a) a natural phenomena and/(b) it is very difficult to get control over it /(c) no error/(d)
o: a natural phenomena and
it is very difficult to get control over it
questions.s: "Phenomena" is the plural form of "phenomenon." Since the article "a" indicates singular, it should be "a natural phenomenon". Use "phenomena" only when referring to multiple occurrences or events.

questions.q: Your son’s-in-law’s / friend is seriously ill / and he wants you / to see him as soon as possible.
o: to see him as soon as possible.
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use ‘sons-in-law’s friend or son in law's friend’ in place of ‘son’s-in-law’s friend.’

sons in law's friend = damadon ka friend

son in law's friend = damaad ka friend

questions.q: His musical skill was evident from a young age, as he could play multiple instruments with ease.
questions.s:
In the context of innate abilities or aptitudes, "talent" would indeed be more appropriate than "skill."

Here's the corrected sentence: "His musical talent was evident from a young age, as he could play multiple instruments with ease."

In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

Mathematics are (A)/ one of the oldest (B)/ subjects in (C)/ the history of humanity. (D)

Although the noun 'Mathematics' ends with an 's', it is not a plural noun. Other such nouns include names of subjects (Economics, Civics, Physics, etc.), names of some common diseases (Measles, mumps, rickets, etc.), names of some games (billiards, draughts), some words like news, ethics, innings, etc. So, we cannot use the plural verb 'are' with the noun 'Mathematics'. So, 'are' should be replaced with 'is' to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q: My grandmother bakes the most delicious loafs of banana bread using her secret recipe.
questions.s:
The word "loaf" refers to a single unit of bread, while "loaves" is the plural form. Since the sentence refers to multiple units of banana bread, the correct term to use is "loaves" rather than "loafs."

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "My grandmother bakes the most delicious loaves of banana bread using her secret recipe."
